 Motor racing-Piastri and Webber part ways in mutual split
 Monday, 09 Nov 2026
 | 7:00 PM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Formula One F1 - Sao Paulo Grand Prix - Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace, Sao Paulo, Brazil - November 7, 2026 McLaren's Oscar Piastri arrives ahead of practice and qualifying REUTERS/Amanda Perobelli 
 LONDON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - McLaren ⁠Formula One driver Oscar Piastri and fellow-Australians Mark and Ann ⁠Webber have ended their management agreement, they said on Monday.
 Nine-times ‌grand prix winner Webber started working with Piastri in 2019 and wasinstrumental in the driverjoining McLaren in 2023 in place of compatriot Daniel Ricciardo and instead of ​remaining withAlpine.
 Renault-owned Alpine had wanted to promote ⁠Piastri to a race seat ⁠after double world champion Fernando Alonso announced he was leaving for ⁠Aston ‌Martin, but the Australian rejected the offer.
 "We are proud to have played a pivotal role in the formative years ⁠of Oscar's career and to have placed him in ​F1 so that ‌he could compete at the front so early in," Webber ⁠said in ​a statement.
 "Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to ⁠a close.
 "This will allow Oscar to build ​on his achievements under a new management structure and for us to embark on our new ventures."
 Piastri, who won back to back titles in ⁠Formula Three and Formula Two in 2020 and 2021, thanked the pair for support and recognised their guidance had been invaluable.
 The Australian has not won a race this season, after looking like he ​might win the championship last year before being ⁠overhauled by teammate Lando Norris and ending up third. Hefinished sixth ​in Brazil on Sunday.
 The winner of nine ‌grands prix has not been on the ​podium for 16 races and is lying seventh in this year's standings.
 (Reporting by Alan Baldwin, editing by Ed Osmond)
